questions.stem: Which output device is specifically designed to produce large-format, high-precision technical drawings such as engineering blueprints and architectural plans?

options.option_text: Inkjet printer — sprays liquid ink droplets onto paper
Plotter — draws precise lines using pens or cutting heads
Dot matrix printer — uses impact pins striking an inked ribbon
Laser printer — fuses toner powder onto paper using heat

questions.explanation: B is correct. A plotter moves a pen (or cutting head) along X-Y axes to draw continuous vector lines, making it the standard tool for CAD blueprints and maps. Inkjet and laser printers render raster images by depositing dots — unsuitable for the continuous line precision required in engineering drawings. Dot matrix printers are impact-based and used for multi-copy forms, not large-format precision work.

questions.stem: An OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) sheet reader used in competitive exam evaluation works on which underlying physical principle?

options.option_text: Magnetic field variations caused by pencil graphite deposits
Differential light reflectance from darkened bubble regions
Electrical conductivity change in pencil-marked paper areas
Infrared heat signature from high-pressure pen or pencil marks

questions.explanation: B is correct. OMR devices shine a beam of light onto the answer sheet; darkened (filled) bubbles absorb more light and reflect less back to the sensor, while blank regions reflect more. This difference in reflectance is detected and interpreted as a mark. Option A (magnetic field) is the principle behind MICR used in bank cheques, not OMR. Option C (conductivity) describes touch-screen technology, not OMR. Option D (infrared heat) has no role in passive paper scanning.

questions.stem: A dial-up modem was essential for early internet connectivity over telephone lines. Which paired function made this possible?

options.option_text: Compressing digital packets into smaller binary bursts for faster transfer
Modulating outgoing digital signals into analog and demodulating received analog back to digital
Encrypting data using RSA public-key pairs before telephone line transmission
Amplifying weakened electrical signals to prevent degradation across phone cables

questions.explanation: B is correct. The word 'modem' is a portmanteau of MOdulator-DEModulator. Phone lines carry analog signals; computers generate digital data. The modem modulates (digital→analog) at the sender and demodulates (analog→digital) at the receiver. Option A (compression) is a separate protocol layer, not the modem's core function. Option C (RSA encryption) is handled by software/SSL, not the modem hardware. Option D (amplification) is the job of a repeater or signal booster.

questions.stem: Which statement most accurately describes the role of L1/L2/L3 cache memory in a modern processor?

options.option_text: Stores the operating system kernel permanently even when power is removed
Acts as high-speed SRAM buffers between the CPU and slower main RAM
Extends available RAM by mapping inactive data to hard disk swap space
Holds BIOS firmware instructions executed during the POST startup sequence

questions.explanation: B is correct. Cache memory (built from fast SRAM) sits between the CPU and main RAM (DRAM). Because RAM access takes ~100 CPU cycles, the cache pre-fetches frequently used data, reducing the average memory-access latency. L1 is fastest and smallest (inside the core), L2 is larger, L3 is shared across cores. Option A describes ROM/Flash (non-volatile storage). Option C describes virtual memory — a software technique using the HDD/SSD. Option D describes the BIOS chip (ROM), not cache.

questions.stem: A digitizer tablet (graphics tablet) is distinct from a touchscreen because it primarily performs which function in professional design workflows?

options.option_text: Converts scanned physical documents into editable text using OCR algorithms
Records audio input and converts it into digital waveform sample files
Translates stylus position and pressure into precise XY coordinate data streams
Displays colour-accurate high-resolution images for professional colour proofing

questions.explanation: C is correct. A digitizer tablet uses an electromagnetic grid beneath its surface to track the stylus's exact X-Y position and pressure level, sending this as vector coordinate data to the software. This enables smooth, pressure-sensitive line work impossible with a mouse. Unlike a touchscreen (capacitive, detects finger touch), it works through the surface and responds only to its paired stylus. Option A describes an OCR scanner. Option B describes a microphone/ADC. Option D describes a colour-calibrated display, not an input device.

questions.stem: A double-conversion online UPS differs fundamentally from a line-interactive UPS in which way that makes it preferred for sensitive data centre servers?

options.option_text: It regulates voltage fluctuations using an autotransformer without touching the AC waveform
It continuously converts incoming AC to DC then back to AC, fully isolating the load from mains
It transfers to battery power only after detecting a complete power outage condition
It filters high-frequency electromagnetic interference injected by other equipment on the supply

questions.explanation: B is correct. In a double-conversion (online) UPS, power always flows: Mains AC → Rectifier (AC→DC) → Inverter (DC→AC) → Load. The load NEVER runs directly off the mains, so any sag, surge, or outage is absorbed invisibly — zero transfer time. A line-interactive UPS (Option A) uses an autotransformer to correct voltage but only switches to inverter on outage, meaning a brief transfer gap. Option C describes a standby (offline) UPS — the cheapest type with the longest transfer time (~8 ms). Option D is a noise filter/conditioner, not a UPS variant.

questions.stem: A storage administrator selects RAID-5 over RAID-1 for a four-drive server array. Which trade-off is the administrator explicitly accepting?

options.option_text: Write performance improves because parity is pre-calculated before disk commits
Usable capacity rises to (N−1) drives, but a second failure during rebuild causes total data loss
Full mirroring is maintained while parity provides an additional recovery layer
All four drives are striped without redundancy, doubling throughput over RAID-5

questions.explanation: B is correct. RAID-5 stripes data with distributed parity across N drives, giving (N−1) drives of usable space (3 drives out of 4 = 75% efficiency). It tolerates ONE drive failure. During the rebuild phase, however, all remaining drives are under heavy read stress — if any second drive fails during this window, the entire array is lost. RAID-1 mirrors data (only 50% efficiency) but survives multiple failures as long as one mirror remains. Option A is wrong: RAID-5 write performance is SLOWER than RAID-0/1 because parity must be computed on every write. Option C describes no real RAID level — RAID-5 does NOT maintain full mirroring. Option D describes RAID-0, which has zero fault tolerance.

questions.stem: ATM receipt printers and Point-of-Sale billing terminals both use a type of printer that requires no ink cartridge, toner, or ribbon. Which technology do these devices rely on?

options.option_text: Inkjet printer that ejects liquid ink onto paper
Thermal printer that uses heat-sensitive coated paper
Dot-matrix printer that strikes an inked ribbon on paper
Laser printer that fuses toner using an electrostatic drum

questions.explanation: B is correct. Thermal printers apply localised heat to chemically coated paper, causing it to darken — no ink, toner, or ribbon needed. ATMs, POS terminals, and supermarket receipt machines all use thermal technology because it is fast, quiet, and low-maintenance. Dot-matrix uses an inked ribbon (older technology), inkjet uses liquid ink cartridges, and laser uses toner powder fused by a photosensitive drum. Candidates often confuse thermal with laser because both are 'non-ink', but laser requires a cartridge while thermal does not.

questions.stem: At a supermarket checkout the cashier scans a product and its price appears instantly. The handheld scanner identifies the product by detecting which physical phenomenon?

options.option_text: Magnetic field variations encoded on the product label
Radio waves reflected by a passive RFID chip in the label
Differences in light reflectance between black bars and white spaces
Infrared heat signature unique to each product package material

questions.explanation: C is correct. A barcode scanner shines a laser beam or LED array onto the barcode. Black bars absorb light while white spaces reflect it back to a photodetector; the pattern of dark/light pulses is decoded into a numeric product code. RFID (Option B) uses radio waves and does not need line-of-sight — it is a different technology used in toll tags and library books. Magnetic variations (Option A) describe MICR used on bank cheques. Infrared heat signatures are unrelated to retail scanning.

questions.stem: A music producer connects an electronic keyboard to a recording computer using a MIDI interface. What does the MIDI connection actually transmit from the keyboard to the computer?

options.option_text: Compressed stereo audio waveforms sampled at 44.1 kHz
Digital event messages encoding note, velocity, and duration only
Analogue voltage signals later digitised by the sound card ADC
Sheet-music notation exported in MusicXML text format

questions.explanation: B is correct. MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) is a performance-event protocol — it transmits which key was pressed, how hard (velocity 0–127), and for how long (duration), as compact numeric messages. It carries NO audio whatsoever; the receiving synthesiser or DAW software generates the actual sound using its own sound engine. Option A describes digital audio (PCM/WAV), which requires a dedicated audio interface, not MIDI. Option C describes an Analogue-to-Digital Converter role. Option D (MusicXML) is notation-software output, entirely separate from MIDI.

questions.stem: A server-room technician installs a KVM switch to manage eight rack-mounted servers from a single workstation desk. Which set of peripherals does the KVM switch share across all eight servers?

options.option_text: Network interface cards and SAN storage HBA adapters only
Keyboard, Video display monitor, and Mouse from one console
Power supply units and UPS battery modules across all servers
GPU cards and RAM modules pooled dynamically across the servers

questions.explanation: B is correct. KVM is the acronym for Keyboard, Video (monitor), Mouse. The switch lets one keyboard, one monitor, and one mouse control multiple servers by switching the signal electronically between them. This saves physical space and equipment cost. Each server retains its own NIC and storage HBA independently (Option A). Power distribution uses PDUs, not KVM switches (Option C). GPU and RAM pooling is handled by GPU virtualisation or NUMA, not KVM (Option D).

questions.stem: A corporate IT team chooses Network Attached Storage (NAS) over a Storage Area Network (SAN) for their branch office. Which statement correctly distinguishes how these two systems present storage to client machines?

options.option_text: NAS uses block-level Fibre Channel; SAN uses file-level NFS protocol
NAS serves files over TCP/IP while SAN exposes raw block storage to hosts
NAS requires a dedicated private VLAN; SAN shares the workstation IP subnet
NAS writes only to WORM optical discs; SAN stores data solely on tape arrays

questions.explanation: B is correct. NAS is essentially a file server — clients access it using file-level protocols (NFS on Linux, SMB/CIFS on Windows) over standard Ethernet/TCP/IP. SAN exposes block-level storage: the server sees a SAN volume as a locally attached raw disk (accessed via Fibre Channel or iSCSI). Option A completely reverses the protocols — Fibre Channel is a SAN technology, NFS is a NAS protocol. Option C reverses the networking requirements. Option D describes specific storage media (WORM, tape) and is unrelated to the NAS/SAN architectural distinction.

questions.stem: A DMA (Direct Memory Access) controller is present in virtually every modern computer. What specific architectural bottleneck does it solve that a CPU-only data-transfer scheme creates?

options.option_text: Translating virtual memory page addresses to physical RAM locations
Moving bulk data between peripherals and RAM without occupying the CPU
Buffering incoming network packets inside a dedicated on-chip L3 cache
Compressing data blocks on-the-fly before writing them to secondary storage

questions.explanation: B is correct. Without DMA, the CPU must fetch every byte from a peripheral (disk, NIC, sound card) and store it to RAM individually — a programmed-I/O busy loop that holds the CPU hostage for the entire transfer duration. A DMA controller seizes the system bus autonomously, transfers the entire data block at hardware speed, and signals the CPU with a single interrupt only when done, freeing the CPU for other work throughout. Option A describes the Memory Management Unit (MMU), a separate component. Option C (network packet buffering in L3) is not a DMA function. Option D (on-the-fly compression) describes a dedicated compression engine, not DMA.

questions.stem: An embedded systems engineer chooses hardware interrupt-driven I/O over software polling for a real-time pressure sensor. Which statement correctly captures the core trade-off that makes the interrupt approach preferable in this scenario?

options.option_text: Polling burns CPU in a busy-wait loop; interrupts free the CPU until an event fires
Polling uses dedicated IRQ lines; interrupts rely on periodic software timer checks
Interrupt service latency is always lower than polling latency across all architectures
Polling is triggered by hardware assertion; interrupts are purely software-scheduled events

questions.explanation: A is correct. In software polling, the CPU spins continuously checking a status register even when no event has occurred, consuming 100% of its cycles on waiting (busy-wait). With hardware interrupts the CPU executes its main program undisturbed; when the sensor asserts an IRQ line the CPU saves context, runs the Interrupt Service Routine (ISR), and then resumes — only reacting when something actually happens. Options B and D reverse the definitions: IRQ lines are the hardware-interrupt mechanism, not a polling resource. Option C is a trap — interrupt latency is real (context save/restore overhead), and ultra-low-latency drivers sometimes deliberately use tight polling loops to beat interrupt latency, which is why Option C uses the absolute word 'always', making it factually false.
